headline: Massie says Senate 'can't run out the clock
dek: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Khanna's own words] Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA) said in a video message: 'In two days, Congress is going to vote to impeach Pete Hegseth.
sources: Rep. Ro Khanna (video message / X / Instagram); Rep. Thomas Massie (CNN The Source, with Khanna); ANI wire via Tribune India / Asianet Newsable / Lokmat Times; Reuters via Dawn / Rappler / Jerusalem Post; IANS via BizzBu
fault_line: Can a president wage war without Congress -- and will this actually remove him? Comment sections split between 'impeach AND remove, jail him for war crimes' and 'the Senate will never convict -- 67 votes is a wall, this

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Khanna's own words] Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA) said in a video message: 'In two days, Congress is going to vote to impeach Pete Hegseth. I'm working with Thomas Massie to lead the charge. We had introduced the Iran War Powers Resolution that would have prevented the war in Iran. Now the voters have spoken. They want us to end this war. That begins with impeaching Pete Hegseth and convicting him in the Senate.' (ANI via Tribune India, Nov 10; Khanna's own Instagram reel, Nov 10 01:36 UTC, 3K likes / 110 comments; Threads post 9.8K likes / 180 comments.) Rep. Suhas Subramanyam (D-VA) also backed removal. [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Massie, on CNN The Source alongside Khanna] Massie warned the Senate cannot 'run out the clock': 'If the Speaker and the Senate Majority Leader are somehow able to push this into the next Congress, for every other bill and resolution, they expire at the end of this Congress. But for impeachments, they go into the next Congress. And so the Senate can't run out the clock on this one.' (ANI via Tribune India, Nov 10.) [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- new number] Massie's office said the vessel strikes had killed at least 243 people, updating the figure of at least 221 in its September summary (IANS via BizzBuzz, Nov 10). [VERIFIED FACT -- procedure and timing] Massie offered the resolution as a question of House privilege; if the Speaker rules it privileged the chamber must act within two legislative days, i.e. a vote by Wednesday Nov 11. Hegseth addresses reporters at a Pentagon press conference Tuesday 8 a.m. Eastern (16:00 ), his first since May. House Speaker Mike Johnson opposes the effort. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- vote outlook] Congressional sources say the resolution may have the simple majority needed to pass the Republican-controlled House (Reuters, via Dawn/Rappler, recorded 0900-01); conviction in the Senate remains unlikely.
sections.what_verified: 3 distinct publisher families with declared tiers: ANI (T1) via Tribune India/Asianet/Lokmat; Reuters (T1) via Jerusalem Post/Rappler/Dawn; Dawn (T3). IANS, BizzBuzz, Asianet Newsable and Lokmat Times have NO declared tier in the registry and do not count toward corroboration; they are cited with attribution only.
sections.what_disputed: Impeachment in the House does NOT remove Hegseth: conviction needs a two-thirds Senate majority (67 votes) while Republicans hold 53 of 100 seats -- Khanna's 'convicting him in the Senate' is an aspiration, not a forecast. No US cabinet secretary has ever been removed by impeachment. Johnson may move to table the resolution procedurally without a straight vote, and Massie himself warned leadership could try to avoid a direct vote. The 243 vessel-strike death figure comes from Massie's office alone -- no independent verification and no breakdown by incident has been published.
sections.why_matters: The Iran war is now eating Washington from the inside -- and it just went bipartisan: a Democrat is co-leading the Republican's impeachment drive against Trump's own war secretary, the vote is Wednesday, and Massie says the Senate cannot run out the clock.
sections.context: Background: FOLLOW-UP to 0900-01 -- Hegseth impeachment goes bipartisan: Democrat Ro Khanna co-leads with Massie; Massie says Senate 'can't run out the clock'; vessel-strike toll now 243

totw_analysis: Our read: The Iran war is now eating Washington from the inside -- and it just went bipartisan: a Democrat is co-leading the Republican's impeachment drive against Trump's own war secretary, the vote is Wednesday, and Massie says the Senate cannot run out the clock. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Can a president wage war without Congress -- and will this actually remove him? Comment sections split between 'impeach AND remove, jail him for war crimes' and 'the Senate will never convict -- 67 votes is a wall, this is theater'.
